newsitem.title: UK: Labour to harness people power for Scots assembly.
newsitem.headline: Labour to harness people power for Scots assembly.

text.p: The Labour Party warned the ruing Conservatives on Thursday not to try to obstruct its pledge to legislate for a Scottish parliament with tax-raising powers within the first year of a Labour government.
In a speech to the party's annual conference, Scottish spokesman George Robertson said Prime Minister John Major had threatened to use the House of Lords to block the proposal.

"The very fact that they are forced to wield the blunt broadsword of the backwoods battalions of the Dukes, the Earls and the Viscounts shows that they have lost the democratic argument and they know it," Robertson said.
He added: "So let me throw down this gauntlet today. If they use the power of the peers, we will use the power of the people and the people will prevail."

Robertson alluded to ructions during the summer caused by the Labour leadership's shifting position on the question of a referendum -- now settled in favour of a two-question plebiscite to be conducted before legislation is tabled.
"We mean business. (Home rule) is going to happen and that's why taking tough decision now makes sense, however bumpy and painful this may be," he said.
